name: Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
description: Target and binding site → candidate discovery and optimization → retrosynthesis → experimental feedback
placeholder: Example: EGFR L858R, ATP-binding pocket; prioritize selectivity and solubility

stages.name: Research Scope and Strategy
stages.instruction: Identify the target, binding site, mechanism, constraints, and data gaps. Define a bounded research plan.

stages.name: Structure and Binding-Site Analysis
stages.instruction: Review structure provenance, conformation, missing residues, cofactors, protonation, and site definition. Specify required inputs when the structure is missing.

stages.name: Candidate Discovery and Optimization
stages.instruction: Plan known-ligand retrieval, library screening, and modifications to supplied molecules. State evidence and validation steps for each proposal.

stages.name: Binding and Multi-Property Assessment
stages.instruction: Assess binding modes, selectivity, ADMET, applicability domain, and multi-objective tradeoffs. Distinguish predictions from experimental activity.

stages.name: Synthesis and Building-Block Review
stages.instruction: Assess retrosynthetic routes, building-block availability, reaction precedents, stereoselectivity, and conditions. Do not invent routes, yields, stock, or experimental conditions.

stages.name: Evidence and Experimental Review
stages.instruction: Review evidence, contradictions, and gaps in prior outputs. Specify experiments and criteria for the next iteration.

stages.name: Research Deliverable and Next Steps
stages.instruction: Summarize actual outputs and preserve capability gaps. Distinguish plans, predictions, and measurements.
